# Review Memo — Corio / Commerce One License & Hosting Agreement (Oct. 29, 1999)

**Perspective:** Corio (licensee/customer). Note at the outset that this is an unusual "customer" position: Corio is buying software *and* a hosted service (MarketSite.net) that it resells to its own Customers under its own EULA and support obligations. That means Corio carries downstream liability it cannot presently pass through. Most of the material risks below flow from that mismatch.

---

## A. Threshold gaps — resolve before signature

| # | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Exhibit E (mandatory End User License Agreement minimum terms) is referenced in §2.5 but not attached.** Corio is agreeing to flow unknown terms into its own customer contracts. | Attach and review Exhibit E. Add: "Corio's sole obligation is to include the Exhibit E terms in its end user agreements; Corio is not liable for a Customer's breach except a failure to enforce after written notice from Commerce One." |
| 2 | **All economics are redacted** ([*] in Exhibit B, §§2.4, 5.5, 13.1–13.2): license fee, Year 2–5 and post-Year-5 M&S and MarketSite fees, revenue-share percentages, resale discount, implementation cap. | Confirm: (a) a cap on annual M&S/MarketSite fee increases (CPI or 5%), *including for the post-termination support Corio is promised under §§5.3/11.3*; (b) rate card protection for §§5.5/13.1/13.2 services; (c) whether the §2.4 resale discount is subject to MFN. |
| 3 | **§10 Confidentiality is entirely outsourced to an NDA "to be concurrently executed."** If unexecuted, there is no confidentiality obligation — including for escrowed source code and Corio Customer data. | Confirm the NDA is signed and attach it. Ensure: perpetual protection for source code/trade secrets; Customer data expressly Corio's Confidential Information; and add security/data-handling obligations for MarketSite (see #8). |

---

## B. High-priority risks

**4. Liability cap is effectively illusory (§9).**
The cap is amounts paid "**for the transaction which the liability relates to** during the twelve months immediately prior to filing" — an undefined, transaction-level cap that could resolve to a few thousand dollars. Combined with the consequential-damages waiver, Corio has essentially no recovery for a service failure that damages its Customer base.
*Fix:* (i) cap = fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim under the **Agreement** (not "the transaction"); (ii) add carve-outs (currently only §8 is excluded) for breach of confidentiality, breach of the license grant/misappropriation of Corio IP, gross negligence and willful misconduct, and payment obligations; (iii) add a super-cap (e.g., 3x annual fees) for breach of the support/service obligations; (iv) expressly provide that **amounts Corio pays or credits its Customers as a result of Commerce One's breach are direct damages**, not excluded consequential damages.

**5. Warranty period is ~60 days from the *Effective Date* and expires no later than Dec. 31, 1999 (§7.3) — i.e., it may lapse at or before acceptance (§3.1 permits testing through Dec. 31).**
The remedy (repair/replace, else terminate and refund *prepaid* fees) is also stated to be Corio's **sole and exclusive** remedy.
*Fix:* Warranty period = 12 months from **acceptance**, re-running for each Update/Upgrade. Delete "in no event later than December 31, 1999." Make the exclusive-remedy language subject to §7.2 (IP), §8, and §11.2. Refund should be **all fees paid**, not prepaid fees, plus reasonable transition costs.
*Also:* §7.3's exclusions are mis-drafted ("The warranty shall **not** apply **only if**: (a) the Software has **been not** properly installed…"). As written the warranty applies only if the Software was improperly installed. Correct it, and narrow (b) from modifications Corio "requested" to modifications actually made by Corio without Commerce One's approval — otherwise the exclusion conflicts with §2.1(v) (Corio's right to modify via Commerce One tools) and §13.

**6. MarketSite.net is a live service with no service levels, no availability commitment, and no meaningful remedies.**
Exhibit C offers "every attempt to contact within 30 minutes" and action-plan targets with **no credits, no resolution deadlines, and no chronic-failure remedy**; staffed hours are 7am–7pm PST weekdays with after-hours coverage for P1 only; only 5 named contacts. Corio must nonetheless provide Tier One 24x7 support to its Customers. The priority definitions also reference "the hosted physical infrastructure," which is *Corio's* infrastructure — allocation is unclear.
*Fix:* Add (i) a monthly availability commitment for MarketSite.net with service credits and a termination-for-chronic-failure right; (ii) 24x7 coverage for P1 **and** P2; (iii) binding response and restoration targets; (iv) a continuing (not 60-day) warranty that the Service will conform to Documentation; (v) more named contacts at no charge; (vi) clean up the priority matrix to reference only Commerce One-controlled components.

**7. No change-control, no-degradation, or end-of-life protection.**
§2.6 gives "unlimited access… **as available to Commerce One customers**" — Commerce One can unilaterally reduce MarketSite functionality, drop MarketPack supplier catalogs, or sunset BuySite. "Upgrade" (§1.13) only captures releases given to the installed base, so a renamed successor product falls into §2.9 ("terms as the parties may agree" = unenforceable).
*Fix:* Add (i) a no-material-degradation covenant, with fee reduction/termination if breached; (ii) 12-month written notice of discontinuation or material change; (iii) a commitment to support the then-current release and the two prior releases; (iv) expand "Upgrade" to include successor/replacement products of substantially similar functionality at no additional license fee; (v) make discontinuation/EOL an escrow Release Condition (see #10).

**8. Indemnity is too narrow and procedurally hostile (§8).**
- Covers only "the **Software**" — **the MarketSite.net Service and third-party MarketPack catalog content are not indemnified**, despite being resold to Corio's Customers.
- Prompt notice and **tender of control** are absolute conditions; no prejudice qualifier.
- Commerce One controls settlement with **its** choice of counsel and no consent right for Corio — it could settle on terms binding Corio or admitting liability.
- The (iii) fallback lets Commerce One **terminate the perpetual license** and refund a pro-rata portion of fees, leaving Corio in breach of its Customer contracts with no transition support.
- §8.2 excludes infringement from "use other than as set forth in the Documentation" or "modification by a party other than Commerce One" — broad enough to swallow the indemnity given Corio's hosting model, §2.1(v) modification rights, and §13 Developments.

*Fix:* Extend the indemnity to the MarketSite.net Service, Documentation, and Commerce One-supplied third-party content; add trade secret misappropriation (the text reads "trade right secret") and any IP right. Notice failure excuses only to the extent of actual prejudice. No settlement imposing obligations, payment, or admissions on Corio without its consent. Corio may assume defense if Commerce One fails to. Before (iii), require Commerce One to exhaust (i)/(ii), give 90 days' notice, permit continued use during transition, refund **all** fees, and fund reasonable migration costs. Narrow §8.2 to combinations/modifications **not** contemplated by this Agreement or the Documentation and not made or approved by Commerce One.

**9. §13.5 ownership carve-back — Corio can lose title to its own work product.**
Developments created **solely by Corio** are Corio's "**unless such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One in which case Commerce One will retain all ownership rights**." The trigger is vague, unilateral, and requires no Corio consent. The final sentence leaves ownership of any enhancement to the Software itself "to be negotiated," with no floor.
*Fix:* Delete the carve-back. If Commerce One is to maintain a Corio Development, Corio retains ownership and grants Commerce One a license, by separate written agreement. Add a fallback: Corio retains at minimum a perpetual, royalty-free, worldwide licence to use any jointly developed or Corio-developed enhancement in the Corio Services.
*Related:* The Corio "covenant and warrant[y]" not to disclose its own proprietary information to Commerce One absent written authorization from a Commerce One Corporate Officer creates breach exposure for Corio in a joint-engineering relationship. Convert to: "Corio has no obligation to disclose…".

**10. §13.6 patent covenant not to sue is extremely broad and one-directional in practical effect.**
Corio perpetually covenants not to sue Commerce One, its **successors and assigns, and all of its licensees, customers and distributors** under **any future patents relating to the Developments** — i.e., Corio surrenders patent rights against Commerce One's entire ecosystem, including competitors of Corio, and the scope ("said Developments") is broader and vaguer than the §13.5 definition. It survives assignment and has no defensive-termination trigger.
*Fix:* Limit to (a) patents claiming inventions actually made in the joint work under §13, (b) the **parties only** (not licensees/customers/distributors), (c) the term of the Agreement plus a defined tail, and (d) terminate the covenant if the other party asserts patents against Corio or transfers the benefit to a Corio competitor.

**11. Escrow protections are thin (§12).**
Release Conditions are limited to dissolution/ceasing business or *repeated* material support breach after a 60-day cure — and **any dispute pushes the release into full AAA arbitration**, during which Corio has no source code. Omitted conditions: bankruptcy/insolvency filing, assignment for benefit of creditors, product end-of-life or failure to maintain, failure to provide the surviving support under §5.3, or change of control to a Corio competitor. The §12.3 license permits use only to "support and maintain" — not to **operate/host** the Software in the Corio Services — and bars subcontracting, which conflicts with §14.8. §12.1 also obliges the *Escrow Agent* to require deposit, rather than obliging Commerce One directly.
*Fix:* (i) Add the Release Conditions above; (ii) make Commerce One's deposit obligation direct, with deposit of each Update/Upgrade, build tools/instructions and third-party component list, plus Corio verification rights; (iii) expedited arbitration (30 days) for release disputes, with no stay where Commerce One has ceased business or filed for bankruptcy; (iv) expand the §12.3 license to include reproducing, operating and hosting the Software to deliver the Corio Services to existing Customers (and new Software Users of those Customers), through permitted subcontractors under NDA; (v) suspend M&S fees after release; (vi) tie failure to execute the escrow agreement within 60 days to a fee holdback or termination right.

---

## C. Medium-priority risks

**12. Perpetual licence vs. termination — internal conflict.** §2.1 grants a "perpetual and irrevocable" licence; §11.2 permits termination for breach; §11.3 preserves rights only for "**then-existing** Customers." §11.3's survival list also omits §2 (the licence itself), §13.5, §13.6 and §11.3.
*Fix:* State expressly that termination does not revoke the perpetual licence so long as licence fees have been paid; permit Corio to add Software Users and Customers for a defined wind-down period; correct the survival list; add wind-down/transition assistance and Customer-data return/portability obligations.

**13. Insolvency triggers *automatic* termination (§11.2).** "This Agreement shall terminate immediately upon notice if **either** party becomes insolvent" — Commerce One's insolvency could extinguish the licence Corio needs to serve Customers, in tension with §12.2, §14.9 and §365(n).
*Fix:* Make insolvency termination exercisable **only by the non-insolvent party**, and expressly carve out Corio's perpetual licence, escrow rights and §365(n) election.

**14. Acceptance testing is time-boxed regardless of delivery date (§3.1).** Delivery is "as soon as practicable" but all testing must conclude by Dec. 30, 1999. Criteria are conformance to **Documentation** only — likely written for on-premise deployment, not multi-tenant hosting at scale.
*Fix:* 30 days from **actual delivery**, with the clock resetting on each re-delivery; absence of notice = **rejection**, not acceptance; add mutually agreed acceptance criteria covering multi-tenant/hosted performance and scalability; confirm refund on rejection covers all fees paid.

**15. Audit rights are one-way (§4.4).** Commerce One can audit Corio, but Corio has **no reporting or audit right** over the MarketSite transaction revenue Commerce One owes it under Exhibit B.
*Fix:* Make §4.4 mutual; require quarterly statements from Commerce One with sufficient supporting detail. On Corio's side, add: audit by an independent CPA under NDA (not contingency-compensated), limited to fee-relevant records, no access to Customer-identifying or competitively sensitive data, 30 days' notice, 3-year lookback aligned to the record-retention period.

**16. Revenue-share definitions invite double-counting.** "Application Management Revenue" is defined as **all** revenue Corio receives from Customers for the Software/MarketSite, with only professional services and network access fees excluded (Exhibit B.2.B).
*Fix:* Add exclusions for hardware, third-party software, Corio's own IP and services, pass-through/reimbursed amounts, taxes, bad debt and refunds; confirm no revenue share is payable on licence fees Corio remits under §2.4; confirm the 3,000-user/40-user-minimum mechanics in B.2.A with the finance team.

**17. Tax allocation is broad (§4.3).** Corio bears all taxes "concerning the Corio Services," excluding only taxes on Commerce One's income.
*Fix:* Exclude taxes attributable to Commerce One's operations, payroll, property and franchise/gross-receipts taxes; require Commerce One to separately state taxes and collect only where legally required and supported by exemption-certificate handling; add standard withholding/gross-up mechanics.

**18. Territory / market-segment constraints.** The licence is North America only; §2.10 only lets Corio "seek permission" (soft "not unreasonably withhold"). §1.1 contemplates *worldwide* Software Users, creating tension for multinational Customers. §1.3 caps Corio's market at Customers under $1B revenue, with above-threshold opportunities merely "discussed as it arises."
*Fix:* Convert §2.10 into an automatic worldwide expansion on Corio's written notice at no additional fee (as the section already contemplates in substance); clarify that Software Users of an in-Territory Customer may access from anywhere; add a Commerce One covenant not to offer hosted/ASP BuySite to Corio Customers during the term (non-circumvention), complementing §2.4.

**19. Restrictions conflict (§2.7).** The no-modify/no-derivative-works prohibition contradicts §2.1(v), §12.3 and §13.
*Fix:* Open §2.7 with "Except as expressly permitted in Sections 2.1(v), 12.3 and 13…".

**20. §7.2 vs. the disclaimer.** §7.2(a) warrants Commerce One is "sole and exclusive owner," yet §7.2(c) contemplates third-party materials; the (partially truncated) disclaimer purports to disclaim implied **noninfringement**.
*Fix:* Reconcile (a) with (c); add an open-source warranty (no copyleft components that would compel disclosure of Corio's code or restrict the Corio Services); state that §7.2 is not subject to the §7.3 Warranty Period and survives; confirm the disclaimer does not limit §7.2 or §8.

**21. Assignment / change of control (§14.1).** Commerce One may assign on M&A without consent unless the counterparty is a "direct competitor" of Corio (undefined). Given Commerce One's criticality, Corio should have more.
*Fix:* Define "direct competitor"; add a Corio right to escrow release and/or termination with pro-rata refund on a change of control to a Corio competitor; preserve Corio's own right to assign in a financing/reorganization.

---

## D. Lower-priority / clean-up

- **§14.3 Arbitration:** add an express carve-out permitting either party to seek injunctive relief in court for IP/confidentiality breaches; require confidentiality of proceedings; consider three arbitrators above a dollar threshold; adopt expedited rules for escrow-release disputes.
- **§14.7 Force Majeure:** uncapped. Add a right to terminate (or suspend fees) if the event exceeds 30 days; exclude failures caused by Commerce One's failure to maintain reasonable disaster-recovery capability.
- **§11.1 Renewal:** 30 days' notice to prevent auto-renewal is tight — move to 90 days.
- **§11.2 "specifications":** undefined; the defined term is "Documentation." Align — this clause is valuable to Corio (a continuing conformance obligation) and should be precise.
- **No refund mechanism on termination for Commerce One's breach** outside §§7.3/8. Add pro-rata refund of prepaid, unused M&S and MarketSite fees.
- **§6.1 Trademarks:** requires immediate cessation of use on termination, yet Corio must keep serving surviving Customers. Add a wind-down licence to use the Commerce One marks as necessary to identify the Software to those Customers.
- **Exhibit D vs. §5.7:** §5.7 says the parties "**shall** engage" in the Exhibit D activities; Exhibit D says they are "**non-binding**." Confirm non-binding governs, and delete or de-fang Item 7 (Corio's 60-day obligation to obtain two Customer orders), which could otherwise be argued as a breach trigger. Also confirm the Item 4 marketing-fund contribution amount is not open-ended.
- **Not addressed at all:** insurance, compliance with laws, export controls, privacy/security standards, incident notification, and third-party audit reporting for the hosted service. Given Corio resells MarketSite to its Customers and will owe them these protections, consider adding at least security, incident-notification and compliance-with-laws provisions.

---

## E. Recommended negotiation priorities

1. Liability cap and carve-outs (#4) and the pass-through of Corio's Customer liabilities.
2. Warranty period/remedy (#5) plus enforceable MarketSite service levels (#6).
3. Indemnity scope, control and the termination fallback (#8).
4. Escrow Release Conditions and the scope of the §12.3 licence (#11).
5. §13.5 ownership carve-back and the §13.6 patent covenant (#9, #10).
6. Change-control / EOL / Upgrade-definition protection (#7) and post-termination fee caps (#2).

I have not assessed pricing adequacy or commercial reasonableness of the revenue-share splits, which are redacted; and my conclusions on flow-down obligations are provisional pending Exhibit E and the concurrent NDA.
